Quoting @ahatamiz1
Gated DeltaNet-2 is here. 🚀
🔥 New paper: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
Gated DeltaNet-2 outperforms KDA and Mamba-3, the latest and best recurrent architectures, head to head at 1.3B. 🏆
💡 Here's the idea behind it:
Linear attention squeezes an unbounded KV cache into a fixed-size recurrent state. The hard part isn't just what to forget, it's how to edit that memory without scrambling the associations already in it.
Prior delta-rule models like Gated DeltaNet and KDA use one scalar gate to do two jobs at once: erasing old content and writing new content. But these two decisions act on different axes of the state, so tying them together is a real limitation.
Gated DeltaNet-2 decouples them.
✂️ a channel-wise erase gate b_t picks which key-side coordinates to read and remove
✍️ a channel-wise write gate w_t picks which value-side coordinates to commit
🔁 recovers KDA when both gates collapse to a scalar, and Gated DeltaNet when the decay collapses too
⚡ still trains fast: chunkwise WY algorithm with gate-aware backward, fused in Triton
📊 Results:
We train 1.3B models on 100B tokens of FineWeb-Edu, matched in recurrent state size, against Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet, KDA, and Mamba-3.
Best average on language modeling + commonsense reasoning, in both recurrent and hybrid settings
Biggest gains on long-context RULER retrieval. S-NIAH-3 jumps from 63 to 90 over KDA, and multi-key needle retrieval climbs from 28 to 38
Joint work with @YejinChoinka and @jankautz.

Gated DeltaNet-2 improves linear attention by decoupling the erase and write operations, addressing a limitation in prior models where a single scalar gate handled both tasks. It uses channel-wise gates to selectively erase old memory and write new content, leading to better performance on language modeling and long-context retrieval tasks.

Experiments with 1.3B models trained on 100B tokens show that Gated DeltaNet-2 outperforms recent architectures like KDA and Mamba-3, especially in long-context retrieval scenarios. The model maintains fast training speed through a chunkwise WY algorithm with gate-aware backward pass, and achieves significant gains in tasks like RULER retrieval and multi-key needle retrieval.

What is speculative decoding?
Speculative decoding is an inference optimization that uses a fast, small "draft" model to quickly propose several future tokens, which are then verified in parallel by a larger, slower "target" model.
This process significantly speeds up the token generation of large language models (LLMs) by allowing the generation of multiple tokens per step, without sacrificing the quality of the output text
Learn more at

🚀 New blog: The next generation of speculative decoding: DFlash and Spec V2
DFlash + Spec V2 hit >4.3X baseline throughput for LLM inference, now the default speculative decoding engine in SGLang! Together with @modal and our jointly-released DFlash drafter for Qwen 3.5 397B-A17B beats both baseline and native MTP in every setting we benchmarked:
1️⃣ >4.3X baseline & 1.5X native MTP throughput (concurrency 1, HumanEval, 8xB200)
2️⃣ Block diffusion drafter: a full token block in one forward pass
3️⃣ KV injection: target-model features fed into every draft layer’s KV cache for higher acceptance
4️⃣ Spec V2 overlap scheduler: +33% end-to-end
Read the code, deploy a DFlash server, and start experimenting!

clean_summary:
Speculative decoding is an inference optimization that uses a small, fast draft model to propose multiple future tokens, which are then verified by a larger, slower target model. This approach significantly increases the speed of token generation in large language models by allowing multiple tokens to be generated per step without reducing output quality.

A new blog introduces DFlash and Spec V2, which achieve over 4.3 times the baseline throughput for LLM inference and are now the default in SGLang. These innovations include block diffusion for full token blocks in one pass, KV injection for higher acceptance, and an overlap scheduler that improves end-to-end performance by 33%. The code is available for deployment and experimentation.
